


In @do_decision_2020, I and my colleagues applied structured decision models to assess agroforestry options for smallholder farmers in Vietnam, emphasizing long-term risks and benefits. By involving local farmers and experts in participatory modeling, the research provided actionable insights while empowering stakeholders to make informed decisions. Our evaluation of the sustainability performance of organic farming systems in Kenya [@kamau_holistic_2021], highlighted the role of agroecology in balancing environmental integrity, economic resilience, and social well-being.

Probabilistic modeling, particularly Monte Carlo simulations, has been central to my work in addressing the uncertainties inherent in agroecological systems. These methods allow for a more nuanced understanding of complex systems by incorporating variability and uncertainty into projections. In @fernandez_prioritizing_2022, I applied decision analysis to prioritize farm management interventions in banana plantations, balancing climate adaptation and mitigation outcomes. In @netter_agroforestry_2022, I used probabilistic tools to evaluate the adoption of carbon offset certification schemes in agroforestry projects, helping project managers navigate trade-offs between economic benefits and environmental goals.

A significant focus of my research has been the identification and promotion of agroecological innovations. In @kuyah_agroforestry_2019, we explored how agroforestry systems in Kenya could reconcile provisioning and regulating ecosystem services, emphasizing their potential to enhance soil health and biodiversity. In @oluoch_integrated_2022, we used participatory approaches to investigate the availability and utilization of wild edible plants in Turkana County, Kenya, highlighting their importance for food security and cultural identity. In @do_adapting_2024 we examined fruit tree-based agroforestry systems in Vietnam, focusing on farmers’ strategies for managing adoption challenges. These studies demonstrate how agroecological practices, when informed by local knowledge and supported by robust decision models, can align with sustainable development goals.

Agroecology thrives on transdisciplinary collaboration, integrating perspectives from ecology, sociology, economics, and beyond. My research exemplifies this approach by engaging with diverse stakeholders—policymakers, farmers, and NGOs—to co-create contextually appropriate solutions. 

A central theme in my work has been the identification of leverage points within agricultural systems. Drawing on Donella Meadows’ concept of leverage points, I have focused on areas where small, strategic interventions can yield significant benefits. Our work in @tabuti_priority_2022, prioritized woody species in Uganda that provide both ecological and socio-economic benefits, offering pathways for sustainable agroecological transitions. In @fernandez_prospects_2020, we assessed the impacts of climate change on Mediterranean fruit production, highlighting opportunities for targeted interventions to enhance resilience.

Ultimately, my contribution to agroecology lies in advancing both the theoretical understanding and practical application of decision support tools in agricultural contexts. By integrating decision analysis, probabilistic modeling, and transdisciplinary collaboration, my work seeks to foster agricultural systems that are resilient, equitable, and capable of supporting both ecological integrity and human well-being. Through these efforts, I aim to empower stakeholders with the tools and insights needed to navigate the uncertainties of agroecological systems and drive sustainable development.

This holistic perspective is critical for realizing the transformative potential of agroecology as a pathway to sustainability, addressing the urgent challenges of climate change, resource scarcity, and social inequality.
